improvements: Mention in the caption that the reading of about 89.9 dB is above the 85 dB threshold, which ties the image directly to the rule.
Note that a dedicated handheld meter is also common, since a phone app is one example among several tools.
grades.reason: The photo shows a sound level meter app with an external microphone reading about 89.9 dB near machinery. It matches the paragraph's measuring tool, and the caption honestly labels it as a generic NIOSH example. The reading is readable at thumbnail size, though small.

figures.learningGoal: Shows what a sound level meter looks like, the tool used to check noise against the 85 dB threshold.
figures.caption: Example of a sound level meter: a NIOSH phone app with an external microphone reading noise near machinery. This is a NIOSH photo, not Utilitek equipment.
figures.alt: A smartphone running the NIOSH Sound Level Meter app with an external microphone shows a noise reading near industrial machinery.

composition.omitted: I added one photo, the clearest sound level meter image I found. I left out the hearing-protection earmuff photos: some showed cold-weather earmuffs, some came from lab tests or were cluttered, and none passed the visual review. The section allows only one image.
